mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a rebound in residential investment, resulting in a short-term positive S&P 500 return over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate sector rotation.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST > previous 3-month average
regime_hint: early recovery phase after demand shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, combined with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS), signals weakening manufacturing and consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo MA AND RSAFS < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 5% indicates a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth above 0.5%) alongside a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above its 6-month average signals robust household demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by >0.5% AND HOUST > 6-mo average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not positive in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for four consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to earnings downgrades and recession risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average, coupled with a simultaneous drop in real retail sales (RSAFS), signals a broad-based supply contraction that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate earnings pressure.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 6-mo MA AND RSAFS < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not negative in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
